items.text: SF's favorite ice cream sandwich just made a big change
items.article: The mint flavor of San Francisco's favorite It's-It ice cream cookie sandwiches has changed color. A major change has come for San Francisco’s beloved It’s-It ice cream sandwiches. The mint flavor of the ice cream cookie sandwich , once an ostentatiously loud shade of green, has changed color, as first spotted by the San Francisco Chronicle. (The Chronicle and SFGATE are both owned by Hearst but have separate newsrooms.) An SFGATE editor bought a box at Andronico’s and confirmed the breaking news — the bright, toothpaste-green ice cream had been drained of color, with a far more muted, pale pastel green in its place. Where the shade once screamed “GREEN!” at the top of its lungs, now, it only whispered. Curiously, though, It’s-It has mostly kept the change quiet. Despite SFGATE’s repeated attempts this week to reach the Burlingame-based company for comment, It’s-It never got back to us. The company has not released any statement announcing the change to its customers, and photos of the mint ice cream sandwich on its website remain the same , advertising the old seafoam green color instead of the new, lighter shade. It’s-It President Charles Shamieh did speak with the Chronicle, telling the outlet that It’s-It made the change due to U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. items.article: Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’ The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life. Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers. “I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push,” Machchhar told Modi in a video call on Friday. “I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realised that if I didn’t get up … then passengers would lose their lives.” His Omani co-pilot apparently stabbed him and set the plane on a steep descent, with the aircraft plummeting about 17,000 feet in the span of a minute. While still being attacked, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter, subdue the attacker and ultimately stabilise the plane. The full circumstances of the attack are still under investigation, but a relief crew on the flight helped land the plane safely in Tabouk, north-west Saudi Arabia . No final finding has yet been made on the motive or on any outside involvement. The incident took place on Wednesday aboard Flydubai Flight FZ1073, which was carrying more than 170 people. While the aircraft was flying over Saudi Arabia, the co-pilot allegedly attacked and stabbed the captain, causing the Boeing 737 to enter a steep descent. The flight was later diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely after passengers and crew intervened. "I think that the state owes me a big apology," Colleen Slemmer's mother said. The mother of the teenager murdered by Christa Pike said she believes she is owed an apology following this week's botched execution in Tennessee. Wednesday's execution attempt came 30 years after Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Pike, 50, the only woman on Tennessee's death row, is in critical condition at a hospital, unconscious and on a ventilator, after her execution failed despite two lethal injections, her attorneys said Friday. Slemmer's mother had traveled from her home in Orange Park, Florida, to Nashville with her husband for the execution, which got underway Wednesday night after a series of last-minute legal challenges. "It's hard. I broke down in tears," the victim's mother, May Martinez, told ABC Jacksonville affiliate WJXX over the phone on Thursday while traveling back home to Florida. items.article: The star also reacted to a bold attempt to set him up with another celeb. Ben Affleck wants potential partners to know he is not currently “prioritizing” his love life. The Oscar winner, 54, told Entertainment Tonight , “It’s just not a big priority in my life.” The actor finalized his divorce from Jennifer Lopez in 2025, after the singer-actress filed to end their marriage on its two-year anniversary. “There’s not a lot of room” for romance, Affleck continued. “I’m not running around… I know what my priorities are. You can’t have two things that are the most important in your life.” His number one, he said, is his kids. “And then I have my work, which I love.” Affleck, who directed and stars alongside Scandal actress Kerry Washington in the upcoming Netflix film, Animals, added, “I’m where I’m at, and I’m great, and who knows what adventures life will bring. I’m open to it, but I’m not trying to chase anything.” According to his three kids, whom he shares with ex-wife Jennifer Garner—Violet, 20, Seraphina, 17, and Samuel, 14—he’s not very good at romance, anyway. “I give advice or try to talk to them like a parent, as you do… but what I’ve found is that now it’s not only one teenager rolling their eyes,” Affleck said on Jimmy Kimmel Live . “I’ll kind of launch into something at the dinner table and now I catch them giving each other looks.
